name: Rear Delt Fly
description: The rear delt fly is an isolation exercise for the posterior deltoid performed in a bent-over position. By abducting the arms horizontally with a slight elbow bend, it directly targets the rear delts and recruits the rhomboids and middle trapezius as synergists. It is valuable for shoulder balance and posture correction.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips until the torso is roughly parallel to the floor. Hold dumbbells hanging straight down from the shoulders with a neutral or pronated grip and a slight elbow bend.
execution.setup_instructions: Use light weight — the rear delt is a small muscle. Bend the knees slightly to reduce hamstring tension.
steps: With a fixed elbow bend, raise both dumbbells out to the sides in a horizontal arc.
Raise until upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly above.
Squeeze the rear delts and retract the shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as arms rise, inhale as they descend.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight, turning it into a row
Extending the elbows too much, losing rear delt isolation
safety_considerations: If lower back discomfort occurs, perform seated or lying on an incline bench
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise until upper arms are parallel to the floor.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Feel the pinch between your shoulder blades at the top
